title: Office of Workforce Development & Innovative Pathways
before:
Workforce Development & Innovative Pathways provides comprehensive coordination and alignment of policies, programs, resources, and initiatives of Adult Education, Career and Technical Education, Education Pathways and Early College, and Extended Learning Opportunities in order to expand learning opportunities for students and elevate the teams’ collective support for Maine’s workforce goals. 

 

Office of Workforce Development & Innovative Pathways Resources
Please visit this page for additional information and tools, including an Interactive
Student Career Discovery Dashboard and workforce resources for schools and students.
 

Adult Education

Maine Adult Education is a public education and career pathways system that enables adults to be prepared for post-secondary education and/or employment. Over 70 adult education programs throughout Maine provide instructional services including high school completion and English language acquisition, to help adults develop the skills for further educational opportunities, job training, and better employment and to realize their full potential as productive workers, family members, and citizens.

  • High School Completion/HiSET™
  • English Language Acquisition
  • Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act
  • Adult Education Provider Listing

Adult Education Home

Career & Technical Education

Career and Technical Education (CTE) provides Maine students with the opportunity for relevant and challenging applied learning to enhance their occupational, personal, and academic success while preparing them to meet the needs of the Maine workforce. CTE offers in-depth training as well as middle and high school exploration into career pathways for ALL students.

  • Perkins V
  • Schools & Programs
  • Resources

Career & Technical Education Home

Education Pathways & Early College

Education Pathways and Early College team oversees the Department of Education’s diploma program which is available to those students who have had their education disrupted and are unable to meet the requirements for a locally awarded diploma. The team works with the University of Maine System and Maine Community College System as well as schools and CTEs to offer early college programming to eligible secondary school students in Maine. Additionally the team works with school counselors, administrators, and other stakeholders in supporting these programs and other initiatives. https://www.maine.gov/doe/pathways/education-pathways-early-college

  • Aspirations Program
  • Educational Disruption Diploma
  • Maine Career Pathways

Education Pathways Home

Extended Learning Opportunities

The Extended Learning Opportunity Program seeks to assist publicly funded School Administrative Units (SAUs) in adopting and/or expanding Extended Learning Opportunities (ELO) Programs in Maine to help Maine youth gain a better understanding of their career opportunities, acquire valuable foundational and 21st Century skills, as well as create meaningful connections to employers in our state.

  • Maine's Life & Career-Ready Standards
  • What Are Extended Learning Opportunities

decisions.label: Remove a line asked for by name

decisions.why: Named in overrides.json for this page. Like the section version, this is one of only two steps here that remove words, and it only ever removes the exact text it has been given.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 1 link on this page opens a file — 1 Video — and says nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Put the card titles on one level
decisions.why: 4 card titles are written at a level copied from an example rather than chosen — h5 on a page whose sections are h2. Only the number changes.

decisions.label: Set a job title the way the rest of the site does
decisions.why: 1 job title sits in plain text under the person's name, where 186 elsewhere on the site are in italics — so the same contact block is drawn two ways depending on the page, and the title runs into the name above it. The standard here is the site's own, not a preference: two thirds of these blocks already do it. No word changes.

decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
